candidates.change_summary: Remove the require that msg.value equals 1 ether, allowing lockInGuess without payment.
Change msg.value requirement from 1 ether to 0 ether, allowing free guesses.
Replace block.number + 1 with block.number so the guess can be settled immediately rather than after one block.
Assign guesses[msg.sender].guess to a zero bytes32 value instead of the hash argument, causing guess to never match.
Delete the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].block so it stays 0, preventing settle from proceeding.
Replace the first require guard with an always-true condition, allowing lockInGuess to proceed when the sender already has an active guess.
Replace the 1 ether msg.value guard with an always-true condition, allowing lockInGuess to proceed with any payment amount.
Replace the stored guess hash with the literal bytes32(0), changing the recorded value used by settle.
Replace the settlement block assignment with one equal to the current block number, changing when settle can run.
Remove the first-call guard that requires the sender's guess block to be zero, so lockInGuess no longer reverts when called again by the same address.
Change the required payment in lockInGuess from 1 ether to 0, so calls with other msg.value amounts complete instead of reverting.
Change the lock block assignment from block.number + 1 to block.number, changing the recorded target block and thus later settle behavior.
Change the first require to check the block number instead of the guess block, allowing lockInGuess to succeed when the stored guess block is nonzero.
Change the first require to check that the guess hash is nonzero instead of the stored block, allowing repeated lock-ins when the stored block is nonzero.
Change the first require to check that the stored guess hash is zero instead of the stored block, allowing a second lockInGuess after a guess hash has been set.
Change the payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to less than 1 ether, allowing lockInGuess to accept underpayment.
Change the payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to greater than or equal to 1 ether, allowing lockInGuess to accept overpayment.
Change the payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to greater than 1 ether, allowing only overpayment.
Remove the payment requirement by replacing it with true, allowing zero-value calls.
Delete the payment requirement, allowing zero-value calls.
Do not store the submitted hash, leaving the stored guess unchanged.
Set the stored guess block to zero instead of the next block number.
Set the stored guess block to the current block number instead of the next block number.
Set the stored guess block to one plus the previous stored block instead of the next block number.
Replace the equality check `== 0` on the initial guess block with `!= 0`, preventing any fresh caller from locking in a guess.
Replace the sent value check `msg.value == 1 ether` with `msg.value != 1 ether`, forcing only incorrect payment amounts to proceed.
Replace the assignment of the guess hash with assignment of `bytes32(0)`, always storing a zero guess regardless of the supplied hash.
Replace the stored target block assignment with assignment of the current `block.number`, removing the intended one-block delay.
Replace the stored target block assignment with assignment of `block.number + 2`, shifting the intended target block forward by one.
Delete the assignment of the submitted hash to the caller's guess, leaving the stored guess unset.
Delete the assignment of the target block, leaving the sentinel block unset so setup is not recorded as complete.
Move the guess-hash assignment after the target-block assignment, reversing the statement order.
Insert an unconditional revert after the assignments, so the function always reverts after executing its state writes.
Replace the require check for an empty existing guess with a check that the caller's recorded guess block equals the current block number, which usually allows a second lock-in within the same block.
Replace the require check for an empty existing guess with a check that the caller's recorded guess block is nonzero, allowing overwriting only after a previous guess has been recorded.
Replace the strict 1 ether payment requirement with a requirement that at least 1 ether is sent.
Replace the strict 1 ether payment requirement with a requirement that more than 1 ether is sent.
Invert the empty-existing-guess guard so a guess can only be locked in when one already exists.
Remove the empty-existing-guess guard so callers can always lock in a new guess.
Remove the exact 1 ether payment guard so the function accepts any payment amount.
Do not store the submitted hash, so the caller's guess remains whatever it previously was.
Store the current block number instead of the next block number as the target block.
Store the caller's guess hash in the block field rather than the next block number.
Store one more than the next block number as the target block.
Store the caller's address as the block field instead of the next block number.
Remove the requirement that the sender has not already locked in a guess.
Remove the requirement that the sent value is exactly 1 ether.
Change the required sent value from 1 ether to 2 ether.
Change the stored block number from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the stored block number from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Change the stored guess from hash to bytes32(0).
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to be nonzero.
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to be exactly block.number.
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to not equal block.number.
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to be greater than block.number.
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to be less than block.number.
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to be at least block.number.
Change the eligibility check to require the sender's block to be at most block.number.
Delete the assignment that stores the provided guess hash.
Delete the assignment that stores the lock-in block number.
Move the block-number assignment before the guess assignment.
Replace the first require in lockInGuess with a condition that is always true, removing the one-guess-per-address restriction.
Change the required payment for lockInGuess from exactly 1 ether to 0 ether.
Store the inverse of the submitted hash as the guess.
Set the unlock block to the current block instead of the next block.
Change the require that the sender has no existing guess to require a nonzero block value, allowing repeated lockInGuess calls.
Change the required payment amount from exactly 1 ether to at most 1 ether.
Change the required payment amount from exactly 1 ether to at least 1 ether.
Change the stored block value from the next block number to the current block number.
Store the hash argument into the block field instead of the guess field.
Swap which struct field receives which assigned value: guess gets the block number and block gets the hash.
Remove the require that msg.value == 1 ether in lockInGuess.
Change the require in lockInGuess from msg.value == 1 ether to msg.value != 1 ether.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 3.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 4.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 5.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 6.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 7.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 8.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 9.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 10.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 1.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 2.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 3.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 4.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 5.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 6.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 7.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 8.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 9.
Change the stored block from block.number + 1 to block.number - 10.
Change the stored guess from hash to bytes32(0).
Change the stored guess from hash to keccak256(abi.encodePacked(hash)).
Change the lock-order initialization to the zero-address guess entry instead of msg.sender.
Replace the require checking that the sender's guess block is zero with require(true).
Replace the require checking exactly 1 ether with require(msg.value >= 1 ether).
Change the stored guess from the function parameter hash to the zero bytes32 value.
Replace the transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Replace the condition `answer != 0` with `answer == 0`.
Remove the `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;` assignment, allowing repeated settle calls with the same guess.
Change the block requirement from strictly greater to greater-or-equal, allowing settlement at the exact block.
Remove the entire if block so that no transfer ever occurs on a correct guess.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].guess == answer` with `guesses[msg.sender].guess != answer`, inverting the payoff condition.
Replace the guess-block precondition with a tautology so settle can proceed when no guess block has been recorded.
Weaken the block-number check to a tautology so settle can run in the same block as lockInGuess.
Use the current block hash instead of the recorded guess block hash, changing when settle can succeed.
Clear the stored guess block before checking the answer, making a second settle call revert differently.
Remove the answer-stored condition so a zero answer can still trigger payout.
Send only 1 ether instead of 2 ether on a successful settle payment.
Delete the require that stops settling before the guessed block has passed, allowing settle to proceed immediately after lockInGuess.
Replace the first require with require(true), removing the lock-in precondition so settle can be called without a prior guess.
Replace the second require with require(true), removing the block-has-passed timing precondition for settling.
Use blockhash of the current block instead of the recorded guess block, changing the answer used to decide payout.
Reset the stored guess block to block.number instead of 0, so the block-zero lock-in precondition remains satisfied differently after settle.
Payout 1 ether instead of 2 ether on a correct guess, changing the observable transfer amount.
Change the settle success condition from answer != 0 to answer == 0, preventing payout for valid nonzero block hashes.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the payout recipient from msg.sender to address(this), making the contract pay itself.
Change the second require to allow settling before the guess is locked, using block.number <= guesses[msg.sender].block.
Delete the guess comparison condition, so any nonzero block hash triggers payout.
Replace the answer check with the literal condition false, so settle never pays out.
Move the reset guesses[msg.sender].block = 0 into the payout branch so it only resets on a winning guess.
Change the blockhash source from the recorded guess block to the current block.
In settle, change the inequality in the answer check from != to ==, so the payout condition inverts when answer is nonzero.
In settle, change the strict block-number check from > to >=, allowing settlement in the same block as the stored target.
In settle, change the zero-check on the guessed block from != to ==, so it settles only when no block was stored.
Change the strict block-number check from > to >=, allowing settlement in the same block as the recorded lock-in block.
Remove the answer != 0 guard so a zero blockhash can trigger the payout if the stored guess is also zero.
Negate the answer-equality condition so the payout happens when the stored guess does not match the computed answer.
Use the current block instead of the recorded block when computing the blockhash answer.
Halve the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Replace the computed blockhash answer with a fixed zero hash, making payout depend on the stored guess being zero.
Invert the balance transfer condition so the payout occurs when the answer does not match the guess.
Remove the answer != 0 guard so a zero blockhash can also trigger payout when it matches the stored guess.
Remove the require that enforces the current block number is greater than the guessed block number.
Remove the require that checks the sender has an active guess.
Replace the strict block-number check with a non-strict one so settle may run immediately when block equals the stored guess block.
Invert the winner condition so it pays when the guess does not match the blockhash answer.
Remove the nonzero-answer guard so settlement can succeed even when blockhash returns zero.
Compare the guess against the current blockhash instead of the stored guess-block hash.
Use the guess hash as the answer source instead of the historical blockhash.
Change the post-settlement reset value from zero to the current block number.
Replace the state reset with a reset of the stored guess hash instead of the block number.
Move the state reset after the payout condition so the reset occurs only after the winner check.
Delete the state reset so the settlement attempt can be repeated.
Delete the maturity check so settle can be called before the target block.
Change the strict block-number check from '>' to '>=' to allow settling in the same block as the recorded guess.
Change the payout condition from checking 'answer != 0 && guess == answer' to only checking 'guess == answer', removing the nonzero hash guard.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 0 ether, making settle never transfer value.
Change the first guard to require the recorded block equals zero, inverting the eligibility check.
Change the hash source from blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) to blockhash(block.number), so settlement compares against the current block hash.
Change the hash source from blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) to blockhash(block.number - 1).
Change the payout comparison from equality to inequality, so it pays when the submitted guess differs from the answer.
Change the nonzero-answer guard from 'answer != 0' to 'answer == 0', inverting that part of the payout condition.
Move the state-clearing assignment 'guesses[msg.sender].block = 0' before reading the blockhash answer.
Delete the state-clearing assignment 'guesses[msg.sender].block = 0', leaving the guess block recorded after settlement.
Change the strict inequality in the second require to a non-strict inequality, allowing settlement in the same block as the guess.
Change the inequality in the second require to equality, so settle only succeeds when block.number equals the guessed block.
Change the first require from checking the guess block is nonzero to checking it is zero, inverting the guard.
Change the reward transfer amount from 2 ether to 0 ether, preventing any payout.
Use the current block hash instead of the committed block hash when checking the guess.
Use the committed block number instead of its blockhash when checking the guess.
Delete the reset of the user's guess block to zero after settlement, allowing repeated settlement attempts.
Change the guess comparison from equality to inequality, paying out on a wrong guess.
Change the nonzero answer check to an equality check against zero, inverting when payout can occur.
Replace the logical AND in the payout condition with logical OR.
Change the strict block number check from '>' to '>=' so settle can be called in the same block as the stored guess block.
Change the strict block number check from '>' to '<' so settle can only be called before the stored guess block.
Change the blockhash lookup to use the current block number instead of the stored guess block.
Remove the zero-answer guard so a zero blockhash can be treated as a winning answer.
Change the answer comparison from equality to inequality so wrong guesses are rewarded.
Delete the reset of the stored guess block before the payout check, allowing repeated settlement attempts.
Change the initial stored-block guard from inequality to equality so settlement only proceeds when the block is unset.
